params.place: on the map: the small piece of Russia alone on the Baltic coast, the rest of Russia far to the east

moments.what: the piece's border traces round and Russia's flag fills it
RUSSIA writes on over the piece
the Baltic Sea's waves ripple and BALTIC SEA writes on
the camera pulls back to the rest of Russia in its flag, a dashed line reaching east from the piece and stopping short
a gap flashes between the piece and Russia

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: This piece of Russia, on the Baltic, doesn't touch Russia at all.

params.place: on the map: Kaliningrad's coast and its two neighbours

moments.what: a pin drops on the city and KALININGRAD writes on
the camera pushes in as the neighbours press in on both sides
Poland fills with its flag to the south
Lithuania fills with its flag to the east
a question mark pops over the piece
the question mark bounces

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It's Kaliningrad, squeezed between Poland and Lithuania. So how did Russia get here?

params.place: on the map: Kaliningrad with Belgium's outline laid over it at true scale

moments.what: the piece's land shades in and its area sign stamps onto the land
trees pop up across the land
fields stripe the land
a sandy beach line glows along the coast
Belgium's outline slides in from the west
Belgium's outline lands over the piece with its flag, the piece showing twice as small

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It covers 15,100 km² of forest, farms and long sandy beaches, about half the size of Belgium.

params.place: on the map: East Prussia a century ago, the era dial turned back

moments.what: the era dial appears at the top of the map
the dial's pointer swings back to GERMANY and the map turns sepia
the old East Prussia paints in with Germany's flag
EAST PRUSSIA writes across it
a castle stands up on the city's spot
KOENIGSBERG writes on under the castle

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Turn the dial back a century, and this land was Germany: East Prussia, with its capital, Koenigsberg.

params.place: on the map: the treaty pen drawing the new line across East Prussia

moments.what: the dial's pointer moves on a notch
smoke drifts over the land
the smoke clears and the German colour fades
a treaty paper unrolls at the top
a giant pen draws a line straight across the land
the line glows from end to end

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then the Second World War ended, and the winners drew a line straight across East Prussia.

params.place: on the map: the two halves of East Prussia, Poland's flag in the south, Soviet red in the north

moments.what: the south half paints in with Poland's flag
the north half paints in Soviet red
a red star stamps on the north half
the coast's water stays blue while ice creeps along the shore elsewhere
a warship and a cargo ship sail into the port

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Poland got the south. The Soviet Union took the north, with its ice-free port.

params.place: on the map: the city's spot, its name sign changed, people leaving west and arriving from the east

moments.what: a red line strikes out the old name on the city sign
KALININGRAD is stamped on the sign
a line of small people with bundles walks off to the west
an arrow draws west along them
small families arrive from the east with suitcases
windows light in the city

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Koenigsberg was renamed Kaliningrad, its Germans were sent west, and Soviet families moved in.

params.place: on the map: the Soviet Union in one red sweep from the Baltic to Moscow

moments.what: the camera slides east
Lithuania fills Soviet red
Latvia fills Soviet red
Belarus fills Soviet red
SOVIET UNION writes across the red land
a road draws on from the piece all the way east
a star pin drops on Moscow

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Back then, nobody minded: Lithuania, Latvia and Belarus were Soviet too, so the land ran unbroken to Moscow.

params.place: on the map: the red Soviet land cracking along its inner borders

moments.what: the dial's pointer swings to TODAY
the red land shakes
cracks run along the inner borders
the pieces drift a little apart
the red drains out of the pieces

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So what changed? In nineteen ninety-one, the Soviet Union fell apart.

params.place: on the map: Lithuania and Belarus in their own colours between the piece and Russia

moments.what: Lithuania fills with its flag
Belarus fills in its own colour
a border line traces round each of them
the camera turns back to the piece
the road east breaks and a gap opens between the piece and Russia

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Lithuania and Belarus became countries of their own, and overnight, Kaliningrad was stranded.

params.place: on the map: the railway from Kaliningrad through Lithuania and Belarus to Moscow

moments.what: a train leaves Kaliningrad station
MOSCOW lights up at the far end
the rails draw on ahead of the train
the train rolls east
a border gate lifts as the train crosses into Lithuania
a second gate lifts at Belarus
the train reaches Russia

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Now, to reach Moscow by land, a train from here crosses two other countries first.

params.place: on the map: the naval port of Baltiysk at the mouth of the lagoon, warships lined up

moments.what: a Russian naval flag rises over the harbour
a first warship slides into its berth
more warships line up along the quay
BALTIC FLEET writes on over the ships
the camera pulls back to the harbour mouth
BALTIYSK writes on beside the port

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Russia even keeps its Baltic Fleet there, in the port of Baltiysk.

params.place: on the map: the piece of Russia filled with tiny people and lit windows

moments.what: the city's board drops in over the piece
tiny people fill the piece as the board finishes counting
more people walk onto the land
windows light up across the land
the camera pushes in as the neighbours dim
the piece's border lights up in Russia's flag
a dashed line reaches east towards Russia and fades

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And 1,029,966 people still live on this lonely piece of Russia, cut off from home.

params.place: on the map: the piece alone on the Baltic again, as the hook opens

moments.what: a Russian flag pops on the piece
Poland's and Lithuania's flags pop beside it
a pointer swings between them
the camera settles back on the hook's framing
the piece's border traces round
the gap east flashes

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Stay Russian, or join the neighbours: which would you pick? Because for now, this piece of Russia is on its own.

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.

references.what: the plan's demand video: a country's strange shape highlighted on the map

thumbnail.pattern: the odd-shaped piece of land lit on a plain map with a few big words; ours lights Kaliningrad in Russia's flag between its two neighbours in our vintage look
